focus: 講設計取捨，分清可逆與不可逆
lead: 今天練的是走過一個系統設計並為它辯護：一句話結論 → 真正的限制 → 架構分幾段 → 自己先點出最弱的一環。加分心法：把決定分成可以回頭改的和不能回頭的，這是資深 PM 最容易被聽出來的一句話。每個 speaking 段落請先出聲講完再看 model answer。

phrases.en: Let me give you the one-line version first, then the reasoning.
phrases.gl: 先給一句話結論，再給推導（讓對方自己決定要不要聽細節）
phrases.ex: Let me give you the one-line version first, then the reasoning: we only upload triggered segments, not full rosbags.

phrases.en: It came down to two options.
phrases.gl: 最後其實只剩兩個選項（表示你收斂過，不是隨手挑一個）
phrases.ex: It came down to two options: upload everything and buy more storage, or triage on the vehicle and upload segments.

phrases.en: We're optimizing for A over B, deliberately.
phrases.gl: 我們刻意優先 A 而不是 B（把取捨講成選擇，不是能力不足）
phrases.ex: We're optimizing for coverage of rare events over completeness of the raw archive, deliberately.

phrases.en: That part is reversible. This part isn't.
phrases.gl: 區分可回頭與不可回頭的決定（一句話就顯出決策成熟度）
phrases.ex: The trigger thresholds are reversible — we can retune them any week. Deleting the raw buffer isn't.

phrases.en: We sized it before we committed.
phrases.gl: 我們是算過才拍板的（用「算過」取代「應該夠」）
phrases.ex: We sized it before we committed: ten cars, roughly 400 GB a day each, against a shared 1 Gbps uplink at the depot.

phrases.en: The reason we went this way is…
phrases.gl: 我們這樣選的原因是 ——（給一個主因，講完就停）
phrases.ex: The reason we went this way is bandwidth at the depot, not storage cost.

phrases.gl: 就我所知 ——（承認資訊可能不是最新，但語氣不弱）
phrases.ex: As I understand it, the vendor's logger can't take custom triggers — Kevin, correct me if that's changed.

phrases.en: Here's the part I'd want you to challenge.
phrases.gl: 主動點出設計最弱的一環（顯得有把握，也搶回主導權）
phrases.ex: Here's the part I'd want you to challenge: the trigger rules only catch scenarios we already thought of.
phrases.fix: 取代 “Any question please feel free to let me know”

phrases.en: The assumption behind that is X — and it's testable.
phrases.gl: 背後的假設是 X，而且驗證得出來（把爭論從立場拉回證據）
phrases.ex: The assumption behind that is that most of the value sits in a small slice of the driving — and it's testable on last quarter's set.

setup: Setup. You're presenting the next-generation data ingest design. The decision you've frozen: the in-vehicle logger keeps a rolling 60-second buffer, a trigger layer marks the segments worth keeping — radar lateral-velocity spikes, hard braking, driver disengagements, and a small rare-object classifier — and only those segments get uploaded. Everything else ages out after seven days and is gone. The constraint behind it is the depot: ten cars at roughly 400 GB a day is about four terabytes a night against a shared 1 Gbps uplink. Alan, the perception tech lead, thinks you're deleting exactly the rare data the program exists to find. David, the program manager, wants to know why you're building this instead of buying the vendor's logger.

prompts.q: Alan: “Take us through the ingest design — and explain why you're deleting data on purpose.”
prompts.frame: One-line decision → the constraint with numbers → the three stages of the design → what gets discarded → name your own weak point.
prompts.say: 先出聲講完整段（目標 50 秒），開場第一句必須是結論，不是背景。
prompts.model: “Sure. One-line version: we triage on the car and only upload the segments the triggers flag — we don't ship full rosbags off the vehicle anymore. The reason we went this way is the depot uplink, not storage cost. Ten cars at about 400 gigs a day is four terabytes a night, and we're sharing a 1 Gbps link, so the cars would still be uploading when they're supposed to be back on the road. We sized it before we committed. The design is three stages: the logger holds a rolling sixty-second buffer, a trigger layer marks segments — lateral-velocity spikes on radar, hard braking, disengagements, and a small rare-object classifier — and then the marked segments plus ten seconds either side go into the upload queue. Untriggered driving ages out of the buffer after seven days. And here's the part I'd want you to challenge: the triggers only catch what we already thought of.”

prompts.q: Alan: “That's exactly my problem. The scenarios that break us are the ones nobody wrote a rule for. You're filtering for the known and deleting the unknown.”
prompts.frame: Concede the real weakness → separate narrow from blind, with one number → name the assumption and say how it's testable → offer a scoped safety net → hand one parameter back to him.
prompts.say: 出聲練習「承認弱點但不失守」—— 不要用道歉或 “I think maybe” 開場。
prompts.model: “You're right, and I'm not going to argue that away — it's the weakest part of the design. Two things though. First, we backtested the trigger set against last quarter's highway data, and it flagged about 94% of the segments our labelers had already marked as interesting. So it's narrow, but it isn't blind. Second, the assumption underneath the whole thing is that most of the value sits in a small slice of the driving — and that one's testable. Pick any set and we'll rerun it. For the genuine unknowns, here's what I can do: keep a random 2% sample of untriggered driving, and hold the full buffer for seven days instead of wiping at end of trip. So if something surfaces downstream inside a week, we can still go back and pull it. That costs us roughly 8% of the storage we just saved, and I'd spend it. Would you want that window longer than seven days?”

prompts.q: David: “The vendor already sells a logger that does this. Why are we writing our own?”
prompts.frame: Show you evaluated it → name the one thing it can't do → give the lead time → state what you're buying vs building → close on what's reversible.
prompts.say: 出聲講一次 build-vs-buy 的說明，控制在 40 秒，結尾落在可逆性上。
prompts.model: “We did look at it, and we're actually keeping most of it. Their capture and upload stack is solid and we're not rebuilding that. What it can't do is take our triggers — the rules are fixed, and a custom trigger from them is quoted at about four months, which lands well after the September cars. So it came down to two options: wait for them and collect blind until Q1, or write the trigger layer ourselves on top of their logger. We're building the thin part and buying the thick part. It's roughly three engineer-weeks, and Ivy already has a prototype running on one car. And that part is reversible — if they ship custom triggers next year we drop ours and switch over, because the interface is the same. What isn't reversible is the driving we don't capture between now and then.”

fixes.bad: Regarding to the storage budget, we already have discussion with the vehicle team.
fixes.good: On the storage budget — we've already talked it through with the vehicle team.
fixes.note: Preposition + noun-heavy：regarding 後面不接 to（regarding the budget，口語直接用 on 更自然）；have discussion 是把動詞名詞化，英文口說直接用動詞更有力。

fixes.bad: This design can let us save 60% storage.
fixes.good: This design cuts our storage by about 60%.
fixes.note: Verb choice：中文的「讓我們……」直譯成 let us 會變成「允許我們」，語氣很弱。用主動、具體的動詞（cuts / saves / halves）並補上 by。

fixes.bad: We choose edge triage because it is more efficiency than upload everything.
fixes.good: We chose edge triage because it's more efficient than uploading everything.
fixes.note: Word form + tense：efficiency 是名詞，形容詞是 efficient；決定已經拍板要用過去式 chose；than 前後詞性要一致，所以是 uploading。

fixes.bad: Actually, actually the main point is actually the bandwidth.
fixes.note: Filler overuse：actually 在英文帶有「其實不是你以為的那樣」的糾正意味，連續出現會讓你聽起來在辯解。想強調重點，直接把它放句首就好。

fixes.bad: If you have any question, please feel free to let me know anytime.
fixes.good: Where would you push back on this?
fixes.note: Register + plurals：question 要複數 questions；而且這種公文式的收尾在口說會議裡等於沒說話。直接邀請具體質疑，你會顯得更有把握，也真的問得到東西。

challenge:
今天在真實會議裡用這一組句型（做到一次就算成功）：

“Let me give you the one-line version first, then the reasoning: ___. The reason we went this way is ___. Here's the part I'd want you to challenge: ___.”

錄音作業（60 秒，手機錄）：挑你手上任何一個系統或流程設計，用英文走一遍。

  • 第一句必須是結論，不准先講背景
  • 中間必須出現一次「這部分可以回頭改，那部分不行」（reversible / isn't）
  • 結尾必須自己點出設計最弱的一環，並邀請對方質疑
  • 禁用：actually 超過一次、regarding to、can let us、please feel free to let me know
check: 我開口的第一句是結論，還是又從背景開始鋪陳？
我今天有沒有把某個決定明確分成「可逆」和「不可逆」兩塊？
被挑戰的時候，我是先承認對方對的部分再給數字，還是急著防守？
